name: implemented-by-migration-sequence
body: The migration order is fixed and executable: (1) the Language node + rooted FQNs land in code; (2) BEFORE any edge migration, every authored `implemented-by` target's rooted destination FQN is declared as a planned Implementation node (`apg plan add <project> planned <kind> <rooted-fqn>`) so the code-ref validator grades it Pending — never Drift; only a `Record::PlannedNode` enters the planned universe (src/artifacts.rs `code_universes_from_export` / src/plan_cmd.rs `task_verb_universes`), a rename `--to` does not; (3) every authored `implemented-by` target is re-pointed bare→rooted via `apg edge rm implemented-by …` + `apg edge add implemented-by …` (atomic per edge, both halves rewritten) — valid as Pending, so `layers::validate_change`'s `InvalidCodeRef` refusal does not fire; (4) the branch is re-scanned; the scanner realizes the planned nodes and `ingest_tree` (`validate_code_refs`) finds every authored target Real — no drift; (5) `apg plan verify` / the next scan confirms no drift and the spine reaches rooted code FQNs. Migrating BEFORE the planned-node bridge cannot resolve — `InvalidCodeRef`, because the rooted destination is neither Real in the old `graph.jsonl` nor a declared planned node — and re-scanning BEFORE the edge migration aborts in `ingest_tree` → `validate_code_refs` with `spec drift: code FQN … is gone from the scanned graph` (after rooting, `scanned_code` holds rooted FQNs while the authored targets are still bare); the planned-node bridge is what breaks that deadlock. Leaving any `implemented-by` target unrooted is a DRIFT defect, not an acceptable pending state.
